## Tours featuring the Los Tucanes trail near Arenal Volcano

The [Los Tucanes trail](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-los-tucanes-lava-trail/) lies in the southwestern sector of Arenal Volcano National Park. The route follows slopes and stretches of hardened lava linked to the 1968 eruption. This is a walking excursion through volcanic terrain; the current itinerary does not include an ascent to the summit.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring this excursion. On the [“Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), Los Tucanes is scheduled for **day 21**. After breakfast, travelers explore the [Arenal hanging bridges](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/), then continue to the volcanic trail. The overnight stay is in the Arenal area.

## What makes Los Tucanes different from other walks in the region

Around [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), different natural attractions can form the focus of a trip. Los Tucanes answers a specific question: what does the landscape look like after a volcanic eruption, and how do lava deposits coexist with tropical vegetation? That is why this excursion makes sense alongside another nature experience rather than replacing every other Arenal stop.

The [hanging bridges](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/) let visitors see the forest at several levels. Los Tucanes focuses on the slopes themselves and old lava flows. The itinerary does not promise sightings of an ongoing eruption, glowing lava, or access to the summit.

If you want a substantial nature-focused journey, compare these two excursions with the [hike to the four El Tigre waterfalls](/costa-rica/el-tigre-waterfalls/el-tigre-waterfalls-hike-horseback/). There, the main experiences involve water, forest trails, and river crossings, while Arenal offers volcanic rock and forest. Each calls for different preparation.

## What day 21 looks like on the longer tour

The preceding day of the [26-day Central America tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/) is spent at the El Tigre waterfalls, followed by a transfer to La Fortuna and time at the hot springs. On the morning of day 21, the group visits the hanging bridges; later, the itinerary continues to Arenal Volcano National Park and the Los Tucanes trail across old lava fields.

This combination reveals two very different natural environments in one day. However, the surrounding days are also busy: on day 22, the journey continues toward [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), including a river section traveled by boat. When choosing a long trip, consider not just the appeal of each stop, but also travel time, opportunities to rest, and whether several active days in a row are comfortable for you.

## Preparing for the volcanic trail

Wear comfortable shoes with good grip, as rocks and soil on natural trails can be damp and uneven. Bring drinking water, protection from rain and sun, and a way to keep camera equipment dry. The precise duration of the Los Tucanes walk is not specified in the excursion terms; it should not automatically be equated with the length of every route in the national park.

Views of [Arenal's summit](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) depend on cloud cover. Even when the volcano is hidden, the forest and traces of old lava remain part of the walk. For access arrangements, permitted routes, and restrictions in the national park, follow the rules in effect before your trip.

## Choosing the right tour

For travelers who want to explore volcanic terrain and nearby natural areas, the key considerations are where the excursion falls in the calendar, the number of active days, and what comes before and after Arenal. On the [larger eight-country tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), Los Tucanes occupies part of one day within a 26-day itinerary. This format makes sense if you are also interested in Mexico, Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, and Panama.

For a trip focused primarily on Costa Rica, start with the [general tour catalog](/costa-rica/tour/) or [adventure itineraries in the country](/interests/adventure/tours/costa-rica/). Check whether the particular tour **explicitly includes** the Los Tucanes excursion, rather than merely mentioning the volcano.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring Los Tucanes

### Can we climb to the summit of Arenal Volcano?

No. The excursion described does not include a summit climb. The route follows the slopes and old lava deposits.

### Will we see active flows of glowing lava?

The itinerary makes no such promise. It visits hardened flows left behind by the 1968 eruption.

### On which day does the excursion take place?

On the [“Central America: 8 Countries in 26 Days” tour](/multi-country/tour/central-america-8-countries-26-days/), Los Tucanes is included on day 21 after the morning hanging-bridges walk.

### Do we need a separate day to travel to the volcano?

On this tour, you arrive in the Arenal area the day before, following the El Tigre waterfalls. The itinerary already includes a night near the volcano before the excursion.

## Excursions in La Fortuna and around Arenal Volcano: bridges and lava trails

[La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) form one of northern Costa Rica's major natural areas. The volcanic cone rises above forests, rivers, and Lake Arenal. In the surrounding region, visitors can look for tropical birds, learn about the history of eruptions, and walk along bridges elevated above the vegetation.

We offer two excursions with different focuses: the [Arenal hanging bridges](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/) and the [Los Tucanes trail across old lava deposits](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-los-tucanes-lava-trail/). The first explores the forest ecosystem at different heights; the second introduces volcanic geology.

## Hanging bridges: the forest from above

The [Arenal Hanging Bridges excursion](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/) takes place in humid tropical forest. The walkways reveal trees and vines from an unusual perspective. Sections elevated above the canopy offer views of greenery and, when the sky is clear, the volcano.

This route appeals to nature lovers. Even without encountering a rare animal, you can study epiphytes, ferns, unusual root systems, and the ways the forest grows in such a damp environment.

An **English-speaking guide** leads the excursion, and guiding services and admission tickets are included according to the selected option. Personal spending and unspecified services are paid separately. The precise combination of bridges, walking distance, and age restrictions should be checked for the chosen date.

## Los Tucanes: the eruption and its hardened lava flows

The [“Arenal: Los Tucanes Trail and Hardened Lava” excursion](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-los-tucanes-lava-trail/) explores the southwestern sector of the national park. It focuses on evidence of volcanic activity and lava formations left by the 1968 eruption. The scenery differs from the hanging bridges: rocky stretches, volcanic slopes, and recovering vegetation.

This is a guided walk with an English-speaking guide. **Climbing to Arenal's summit is not included**; visitors use the designated national park trails.

Do not expect to see a current flow of glowing lava. The volcano has gone through different stages of activity over the years, while conservation authorities determine which areas are safe to visit. The history of eruptions is part of the guide's explanation, not a promise of a dramatic event.

## What to choose around Arenal

| Interest | Excursion |
|---|---|
| Tropical forest | Hanging bridges |
| Volcanic geology | Los Tucanes |
| Views of Arenal | In clear weather |

If you would like to spend time among the vegetation and listen for birds, choose the [hanging-bridges walk](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/). To learn about the volcano's features and past activity, choose the [lava trail](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-los-tucanes-lava-trail/).

Other natural attractions in the La Fortuna area include the waterfall of the same name and hot springs. Their presence in the region **does not mean they are included** in the two excursions described; they require a separate itinerary.

## Weather, exertion, and wildlife viewing

Tropical rain can fall at any time, and clouds often conceal Arenal's summit. Shoes with good traction, a raincoat, water, and protection for camera equipment will make the forest walk more comfortable. Stable soles are particularly important on the lava-covered sections.

Spotting toucans, sloths, or monkeys depends on natural conditions and luck. Even the name Los Tucanes does not guarantee the birds will appear in front of the group. Keep your distance, do not feed animals, and stay on permitted paths.

Explore other journeys in the [Costa Rica tour catalog](/costa-rica/tour/) and our [selection of nature trips](/interests/wildlife/).

## Frequently asked questions about excursions near Arenal Volcano

### Is there a hanging-bridges walk?

Yes. Our selection includes a [separate Arenal hanging-bridges excursion](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/) with an English-speaking guide.

### Can we climb to the volcano's summit?

The [Los Tucanes excursion](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-los-tucanes-lava-trail/) includes a walk across hardened lava deposits. A summit ascent is not part of the itinerary.

### Will we see flowing lava?

There is no basis for promising an active lava flow. The excursion focuses on traces of past eruptions and the volcanic landscape.

### Which excursion is best for wildlife?

Start with the [forest walk on the bridges](/costa-rica/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/arenal-hanging-bridges-forest-walk/), although encounters with particular animals cannot be guaranteed.

## Monteverde and Viento Fresco Waterfalls: a full day in the mountain forests

[Monteverde and Santa Elena](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) are known for the cloud forests of the Cordillera de Tilarán. At elevation, moist air forms mist that lingers among the trees, ferns, and epiphytes. The Ada Tours excursion adds a visit to the **Viento Fresco waterfalls** to this mountain landscape.

Departure is **early in the morning**, and the trip takes **approximately 12 hours**. It is a long day involving travel, walking, and time by the water. The main appeal is the combination of mountain forest with several waterfalls, rather than a short circuit inside a single reserve.

## What is a cloud forest?

Unlike the hot forests of the lowlands, mountain cloud forests are often shrouded in mist. Moisture settles on leaves, trunks, and mosses, so even an ordinary walk feels like moving beneath a dense green canopy. Ferns, mosses, orchids, and other epiphytes grow on the trees.

These forests are important habitats for birds, insects, and small animals. Exploring them begins with the forest itself: signs of moisture, unusual roots, and changing plant communities. **An encounter with a particular bird or animal species cannot be guaranteed.** Wildlife-viewing conditions vary from day to day.

The Monteverde region contains several protected areas and privately operated visitor facilities. A route to Viento Fresco and a walk specifically inside the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve are not automatically the same visit. This excursion includes mountain forest and waterfalls, but admission to the biological reserve itself should be confirmed separately.

## Viento Fresco Waterfalls: trails, cascades, and time to relax

The itinerary continues to Viento Fresco Waterfalls. It includes Víctor Álvarez's farm, **5 waterfalls**, forest trails, and the possibility of relaxing by the water.

The paths between the waterfalls cross uneven terrain. After rain, trails may become slippery and currents stronger. Bring hiking shoes with good grip, lightweight waterproof clothing, and dry clothes to change into. Before walking to the waterfalls, consider current trail conditions and your own physical readiness.

Swimming, cave exploration, and horseback riding may also be possible. These are **activities potentially available at the complex**; whether they are included in the specific price and available on the day must be confirmed separately. Swimming conditions are especially important: safety depends on water levels and local guides' decisions, not merely the date.

## Lunch and planning a long excursion day

The excursion concludes with **a traditional lunch at the complex's restaurant**. Lunch is part of the day's sequence; the menu, drinks, and any dietary requirements should be discussed when booking.

Because of the trip's length, it helps to know the departure and return points, the start of the walks, and the actual walking distance in advance. If you want to devote more time to birdwatching or photography, that will influence the choice of stops. Completing every activity available at the complex in one day is not promised.

This excursion particularly suits travelers who want to experience several characteristic Costa Rican natural settings on one trip: humid mountain forest, rivers, and waterfalls. Compare it with the [separate Monteverde cloud forest walk](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-cloud-forest-reserve-walk/), which has a different focus: the ecosystem of the biological reserve.

For related choices, see our [nature and wildlife trips](/interests/wildlife/) and the [Costa Rica excursion catalog](/costa-rica/excursion/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Viento Fresco trip

### How long does the excursion take?

The description gives **approximately 12 hours** with an early start. The exact start of the walks and time of return depend on the agreed logistics.

### How many waterfalls are mentioned in the itinerary?

The complex has **5 waterfalls**. Whether all trails can be completed on a given day depends on their condition.

### Can we swim beneath the waterfalls?

Swimming is listed as a possible activity, but it depends on water levels, applicable rules, and actual safety conditions.

### Is horseback riding included?

It is mentioned as an available activity. Whether it is included in the price must be confirmed separately.

### Is a meal provided?

The itinerary ends with a traditional lunch at the complex's restaurant. The specific menu is arranged separately.

## Which tour includes an option to visit Monteverde and Viento Fresco?

The [“Monteverde Cloud Forest and Viento Fresco Waterfalls” excursion](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/costa-rica-monteverde-viento-fresco-day-trip/) is associated with the [12-day Costa Rica–Nicaragua VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/). On that journey, the trip to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) takes place **instead of the main program on day three**, not as a mandatory addition to excursions already scheduled.

The regular day's program includes a chocolate experience, a walk on the slopes of Arenal Volcano, and a folklore performance. The alternative heads to the cloud forest and waterfalls and occupies much of the day. The two options differ in subject and timing.

## What makes the waterfall excursion appealing

The separate excursion lasts around 12 hours and starts early in the morning. It covers mountain forest, the grounds of Víctor Álvarez's farm, and the [Viento Fresco Waterfalls](/costa-rica/place/viento-fresco-waterfalls/). The description mentions five waterfalls, forest trails, and the possibility of swimming; caves and horseback riding are also listed as options. A traditional lunch concludes the visit.

The phrase **“you can choose”** is important. It means activities are available at the site, not that every trail, swimming opportunity, cave, and horseback ride is guaranteed within a single excursion. Their inclusion, duration, and conditions must be agreed for the particular group.

The waterfall trip differs from the [walk in Monteverde's biological reserve](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-cloud-forest-reserve-walk/): these are two separate excursion products in the same region. One focuses on waterfalls and active experiences; the other on the protected forest ecosystem and observation.

## Choosing day three: Arenal or the cloud forest

| Option | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Arenal | Cacao, volcanic trails, folklore |
| Monteverde | Forest, waterfalls, an extended day trip |

If waterfalls and natural trails appeal to you most, Monteverde can be a worthwhile alternative. Travelers who want to learn more about cacao and the [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) region may prefer the original day's program.

After these excursions, the two-country journey continues through Costa Rica's natural regions to Nicaragua, with [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), Masaya Volcano, and Apoyo Lagoon among the stops. The main tour includes private flights between the countries, but that does not mean the separate waterfall excursion automatically provides the same transport or additional options.

Before confirming the itinerary, we can agree on the exact day-three option, travel time, and chosen activities. Closed shoes, a rain jacket, and a change of clothing are useful for a long walk through humid forest.

## Frequently asked questions about the tour featuring Viento Fresco

### Are the waterfalls part of the standard day-three program?

No. On the VIP tour, this is an alternative excursion replacing the main program of chocolate, volcano, and folklore experiences.

### Can all five waterfalls be visited in one excursion?

The complex has five waterfalls, but the actual route depends on the selected activities and conditions on site. The excursion as a whole lasts about 12 hours.

### Where does the journey continue afterward?

After the Costa Rican section, the tour continues into Nicaragua with historic and natural stops and time relaxing by Apoyo Lagoon.

## Excursions in Monteverde and Santa Elena: cloud forest and waterfalls

[Monteverde and Santa Elena](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/) lie in the Cordillera de Tilarán mountains. Moist air and clouds create an environment where trees are covered in mosses, vines, and epiphytes. Travelers come to walk through cloud forest, look for birds, and explore waterfalls on forested slopes.

Ada Tours offers several **distinct excursion formats**: a nature walk, a canopy experience, the Viento Fresco waterfall route, and an El Tigre hike. They vary in duration, physical demands, and itinerary. When choosing, first decide whether you want quiet forest observation or a more active experience.

## Walking through the cloud forest

The [“Monteverde: Cloud Forest Walk” excursion](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-cloud-forest-reserve-walk/) follows trails in a natural area at approximately 1,500 meters above sea level. Its focus is the humid mountain-forest ecosystem, where mist supports the growth of mosses, ferns, and diverse epiphytes.

An **English-speaking guide** leads the excursion and explains the characteristics of the forest. Birdwatching takes patience: quetzals and other notable species appear according to the season and weather, and sightings cannot be guaranteed.

Monteverde's nature reserve itself offers several walking options along its own trails, from relatively short walks to longer routes. These independently operated reserve options should not automatically be attributed to the Ada Tours excursion. The confirmed conditions of the particular product apply.

## Canopy tour: an active experience above the forest

The [Monteverde canopy tour](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-canopy-forest/) is a separate activity. Participants follow a purpose-built route through the forest using safety harnesses and the operator's facilities. Unlike a normal walk, health, height, or weight restrictions and equipment rules may be significant.

The route specifications and operator are confirmed separately before the journey. Clarifying these details is more valuable than promotional promises about a particular zip-line length. The service language stated in the description is English.

A canopy tour suits travelers looking for an energetic forest experience. Those who prefer unhurried plant photography and birdwatching are better served by the [regular forest walk](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-cloud-forest-reserve-walk/).

## Viento Fresco: waterfalls and forest trails

The [“Monteverde Cloud Forest and Viento Fresco Waterfalls” excursion](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/costa-rica-monteverde-viento-fresco-day-trip/) is a roughly 12-hour program with an early departure. It combines the Monteverde mountain scenery with the forest surroundings of the Viento Fresco waterfall complex.

Its description includes forest trails, waterfalls, opportunities for swimming, and alternative activities around the farm. The visit ends with a traditional lunch. Actual swimming access and optional activities depend on conditions that day; availability at the complex does not imply each activity is included in the paid package.

This is an option for travelers who want to devote most of the day to nature and combine walking with waterfall visits.

## El Tigre: a hike followed by horseback riding

The [“El Tigre: Four Waterfalls and Horseback Riding” excursion](/costa-rica/el-tigre-waterfalls/el-tigre-waterfalls-hike-horseback/) follows forest paths and rocky sections. The itinerary includes approximately three hours of moderately to highly demanding hiking, followed by a horseback ride lasting around 35 minutes.

Along the way, there are crossings of small streams and river sections. The trip suits physically prepared travelers who are comfortable with wet trails and uneven ground. If rain intensifies, safety on rocks and at water crossings becomes especially important.

This is a standalone program; it should not be mistaken for an ordinary short walk through the Monteverde reserve.

## How to choose an excursion in Monteverde

| Preference | Program |
|---|---|
| Birds and plants | Cloud forest |
| Active experience at height | Canopy |
| Full-day waterfalls | Viento Fresco |
| Hiking | El Tigre |

If you have only a few hours, start with the [forest walk](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-cloud-forest-reserve-walk/). If you want several waterfalls and a full day out, consider [Viento Fresco](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/costa-rica-monteverde-viento-fresco-day-trip/). For a more demanding hike, [El Tigre](/costa-rica/el-tigre-waterfalls/el-tigre-waterfalls-hike-horseback/) may be more appealing.

## Weather and visiting conditions

Mist and humidity are a normal part of Monteverde's environment. A raincoat, waterproof footwear, and a cover for camera equipment are useful even during the relatively drier season. Temperatures at altitude can be cooler than on Costa Rica's coast.

Binoculars help with birdwatching, while shoes with good tread are important for hikes with water crossings. Do not feed or chase animals to get a photograph. In protected forests, follow marked trails and your guide's instructions.

Compare suitable journeys in the [Costa Rica catalog](/costa-rica/tour/) and the [adventure travel collection](/interests/adventure/).

## Frequently asked questions about excursions in Monteverde

### Can we see a quetzal on the walk?

A sighting is possible but not guaranteed. The [cloud forest excursion](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-cloud-forest-reserve-walk/) focuses on the entire ecosystem, not just one bird.

### Does Monteverde offer a canopy tour?

Yes. We offer a [separate canopy tour](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/monteverde-canopy-forest/) with English-speaking support. The route and restrictions are confirmed when booking.

### Which waterfall route is more active?

[El Tigre](/costa-rica/el-tigre-waterfalls/el-tigre-waterfalls-hike-horseback/) involves around three hours of hiking on challenging terrain and a horseback ride. [Viento Fresco](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/costa-rica-monteverde-viento-fresco-day-trip/) is a long combined excursion with different activities.

### Can forest and waterfalls be combined?

Yes, they are combined in the [Monteverde and Viento Fresco itinerary](/costa-rica/monteverde-santa-elena/costa-rica-monteverde-viento-fresco-day-trip/). The trip lasts approximately 12 hours.
